body.x: CES 2027 will have its largest mobility footprint ever, with more than 350,000 square feet of vehicle tech exhibits. The show runs from Jan. 6 to Jan. 9, 2027, in Las Vegas. The plan was announced Nov. 2 at a media event in Detroit.

AI, advanced computing, connectivity and automation are drawing several industries together. Autonomous transportation, aviation, marine technology, heavy machinery and connected infrastructure now form an increasingly connected mobility ecosystem. That is creating new opportunities across transportation, technology, energy and infrastructure.

CES 2027 will reflect that shift on the show floor. Exhibits and experiences will fill the West Hall, Central Plaza and other areas, and keynote and conference stages will carry the discussion. Visitors will see cars that think, vehicles defined by software and robotaxis moving through cities. They will also see AI transforming the driving experience and intelligent machines reinventing how people, goods and entire industries move.

The announced lineup includes AMD, Aptiv, BMW, Bosch, Brunswick, Caterpillar, Corning, Emotiv, Ford, FORVIA, Garmin, Geely Auto, John Deere, Kia Corporation, KPIT Technologies Ltd., KPMG LLP, LG Innotek, Michigan State University, MinebeaMitsumi, Oshkosh, Quanttronix, Sonatus, Stellantis, Taktotek, Uber, Valeo, Waymo, Yazaki Innovations, Inc. and more.

Gary Shapiro, Executive Chair of the Consumer Technology Association (CTA)®, which owns and produces CES, called it "the most impressive lineup of mobility innovators I've ever seen at the show." He said the companies defining the future of transportation are coming to CES, from automakers and autonomy leaders to software, AI, chips, heavy equipment and infrastructure. Anyone who wants to see where mobility is headed, he said, needs to be at CES 2027.

Mobility will be in the spotlight from the opening days. Tekedra Mawakana, Co-CEO of Waymo, will give a keynote on Tuesday, Jan. 5, at 6:30 p.m. Antonio Filosa, CEO of Stellantis, will take the stage on Wednesday, Jan. 6, at 8:30 a.m., after the State of the Industry Address. The conversation will continue all week on the Mobility Stage, presented by Bosch, and in conference programming on the technologies and business models changing transportation.
Mobility companies will also draw attention during CES Media Days on Jan. 4 and Jan. 5. Media get an early look at the announcements and technologies expected to shape the industry in the year ahead.

The mobility conference program runs across three tracks. On Wednesday, Jan. 6, the Connect2Car: Connected Vehicle Intelligence Track covers "AI, Cybersecurity, and the Price of Trust in Connected Mobility," "Beyond the Dashboard: Rethinking the In-Vehicle Interface," "Frictionless Mobility: Reimagining In-Vehicle Transactions," "From Garage to Global: Scaling Mobility Innovation," "Permission to Act: Agentic AI and Accountability in the Vehicle" and "SDV at Scale: Why Standard Data Decides Who Ships Faster."

On Thursday, Jan. 7, the Vehicle Tech and Advanced Mobility Track covers "5G Lite: Expanding Automotive Connectivity Horizons," "Cars Rewritten: The Software Revolution," "EVs as Energy Assets," "Robotaxis and Beyond: AV Business Models Taking Shape," "Safe Freight at Scale: The Road to Autonomous Deployment," "Simulating the Road Ahead" and "Turning Vehicle Data Into Value." On Friday, Jan. 8, the Resilient Communities Track covers "Technology Shaping Smarter Cities" and "The Future of Micromobility."

CES 2026 drew more than 15,000 mobility industry attendees, and 60% of them were senior executives. At CES 2027, automakers, suppliers, software and semiconductor companies, startups, investors, policymakers and technology leaders will again come together in one place. They will launch products, build partnerships, meet customers and see where the global mobility market is headed next.

CES features every aspect of the tech sector and is owned and produced by CTA, North America's largest technology trade association. CES 2027 runs from Jan. 6 to Jan. 9, 2027, in Las Vegas. CTA says its members, from startups to global brands, help support more than 17 million American jobs.
